vn_background_tasks.description: Canonical provider and model used by cache-sharing post-turn plugin tasks.

writer.description: The primary storyteller. Responsible for prose generation, scene flow, and maintaining narrative voice through the 'Main' model tier.
writer.disabled_behavior: This module is critical and cannot be disabled.

wizard.label: Writer
wizard.author_note: This is the engine's voice. Spend your best model budget here first.
wizard.enabled_note: The Writer creates the prose, scene flow, and immediate narrative response.
wizard.settings_note: Tune provider and model routing in Settings once your first project is running.

summarizer.description: Historical memory specialist. Compresses past scenes into concise summaries and keeps character sheets updated to maintain long-term consistency.
summarizer.disabled_behavior: Long-term memory updates are paused. Past turns will not be condensed, and character profile updates will be deferred.

wizard.label: Summarizer
wizard.author_note: Keep this on for long campaigns. It is one of the quiet systems that makes Fablekin feel less forgetful.
wizard.enabled_note: Past scenes are condensed into summaries and synopses for future context.
wizard.disabled_note: The story still runs, but long-term memory artifacts stop being refreshed.
wizard.settings_note: Use cheaper aliases here once your main Writer and Director are stable.

director.description: High-level scene orchestrator. Analyzes the current context to provide specific narrative directives and guidance to the Writer before generation begins.
director.disabled_behavior: The engine will skip strategic scene review. The Writer will generate content directly from the history and active memory blocks without additional guidance.

wizard.label: Director
wizard.author_note: Recommended. The Director is what makes the Writer feel like it has a plan instead of only reacting.
wizard.enabled_note: Each turn receives strategic guidance before prose generation.
wizard.disabled_note: The Writer works directly from memory and lore without a planning pass.
wizard.settings_note: Use a fast high-end model if latency becomes annoying.

asset_selector.description: Visual and auditory curator. Evaluates the scene content to select appropriate backgrounds, sprites, and music (OST) tracks from your asset database.
asset_selector.disabled_behavior: Automated asset curation is bypassed. The scene will maintain its current state or use hardcoded defaults for music and backgrounds.

wizard.label: Asset Selector
wizard.author_note: Keep this on if you have backgrounds and music. It is a cheap way to make scenes feel staged.
wizard.enabled_note: The engine chooses backgrounds and OST tracks based on the scene.
wizard.disabled_note: Automated background and music selection are skipped.
wizard.settings_note: Fine-tune OST and background behavior in the Engine Management settings.

emotion_classifier.description: Micro-expression specialist. Analyzes dialogue lines to determine the most fitting character moods for sprite selection and gaze direction.
emotion_classifier.disabled_behavior: Mood classification is bypassed. All characters will default to a 'neutral' emotional state for sprite selection and TTS generation.

wizard.label: Emotion Classifier
wizard.author_note: Recommended for VN-style play. Sprite moods are a big part of the scene feeling alive.
wizard.enabled_note: Dialogue lines receive emotion labels for sprite and TTS routing.
wizard.disabled_note: Characters fall back to neutral presentation more often.
wizard.settings_note: If this gets expensive, move it to a cheaper fast model before turning it off.

dialogue_processor.description: Syntactic refinement engine. Processes raw LLM output to clean dialogue tags, format text, and prepare content for the VN viewer interface if the Writer does not already do so.
dialogue_processor.disabled_behavior: Syntactic cleanup is disabled. Raw LLM output is used directly, which might include unformatted dialogue tags or thinking blocks.

wizard.label: Dialogue Processor
wizard.author_note: Useful safety net. It keeps raw model output from leaking awkward formatting into the VN layer.
wizard.enabled_note: Generated text is cleaned and prepared for the viewer pipeline.
wizard.disabled_note: Raw Writer output is used more directly.
wizard.settings_note: Keep it fast; this should not be one of the expensive calls.

memory_retriever.description: Cognitive RAG specialist. Generates intelligent search queries to retrieve relevant lore chunks and historical facts from the vector database.
memory_retriever.disabled_behavior: Automated RAG lookups are disabled. The engine will rely only on the immediate context window without searching the lore database.

wizard.label: Memory Retriever
wizard.author_note: Recommended once Ollama is reachable. This is the difference between context window memory and project memory.
wizard.enabled_note: The engine searches lore and old story chunks for relevant details.
wizard.settings_note: If retrieval feels noisy, tune Memory Management rather than disabling this first.

gaze_director.description: Cinematography assistant. Determines where characters should be looking during dialogue based on the active speaker and scene dynamics. Only active if there are directional sprites.
gaze_director.disabled_behavior: Gaze direction analysis is skipped. Characters will maintain their current rotation or default to 'front' facing during all dialogue.

wizard.label: Gaze Director
wizard.author_note: Nice when your sprites support direction. Harmless but less important if your assets are mostly front-facing.
wizard.enabled_note: Characters can look toward speakers or scene targets.
wizard.disabled_note: Characters keep default or existing facing directions.
wizard.settings_note: Only matters when directional sprite assets exist.

sprite_variant_orchestrator.description: Visual continuity specialist. Analyzes scene context to select the most appropriate character sprite variants (costumes, forms, etc.) based on the narrative situation. Only active if there are variant sprites.
sprite_variant_orchestrator.disabled_behavior: Variant selection is disabled. Characters will always use their 'default' sprite configuration regardless of the narrative context.

wizard.label: Sprite Variant Orchestrator
wizard.author_note: Keep this on if characters have outfits, forms, or scene-specific variants.
wizard.enabled_note: The engine chooses appropriate sprite variants based on context.
wizard.disabled_note: Characters stay on default variants unless another system changes them.
wizard.settings_note: This is most valuable after your sprite library grows.

scene_phase_classifier.description: Post-writer gameplay handoff classifier. Evaluates the generated chapter and decides whether a registered gameplay capability should take over the unresolved scene boundary.
scene_phase_classifier.disabled_behavior: Gameplay handoff confirmation is skipped. Scene phase remains NORMAL unless other modules set it explicitly.

wizard.label: Scene Phase Classifier
wizard.author_note: Keep this on if you use gameplay or interlude plugins. It helps decide when the story should hand off.
wizard.enabled_note: Generated chapters can trigger registered gameplay or interlude capabilities.
wizard.disabled_note: Scene phase remains normal unless another module sets it explicitly.
wizard.settings_note: Tune confidence only after seeing real handoff behavior.

gender_classifier.description: Utility auditor. Identifies character gender for linguistic agreement and specialized asset routing (e.g., TTS voice gender).
gender_classifier.disabled_behavior: Gender detection is skipped. The system will use default linguistic agreements and generic voice routing for unknown characters.

wizard.label: Gender Classifier
wizard.author_note: Small helper. It mostly improves generic sprite and voice routing for unknown characters.
wizard.enabled_note: Unknown characters can receive gender-aware fallback routing.
wizard.disabled_note: Unknown characters use neutral/default routing unless facts already exist.
wizard.settings_note: This should usually stay on because it is cheap.

tts_core.custom_moods: neutral, happy, sad, angry, surprised, fearful, caring
